prize_parts.citation: for showing how firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting shape the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration changed from B001 in round 1 to B048 now. In round 1 I chose B001 with moderate confidence and named B048 as my first alternative. I said then that B001 would not compete on identification strength and that B048 had the cleaner two-name attribution and firm-level replication. The exchange has not given me a way to rebut either point. The B001 defences say the lasting contribution is the cross-country data, the research design and the established regularities. I accept that. But a citation resting on those still has to name three people and leave out Vishny, a co-author of the founding papers, and Shleifer's wider portfolio blurs where the credit ends. B048 does not carry those costs to the same degree. Melitz (2003) is the identifiable originating model. Helpman, through the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple exporting-versus-FDI work and his earlier trade theory, is the natural second name. The qualitative predictions (selection into exporting, exporter productivity premia, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm and customs data across many countries for over twenty years. My own work on pricing, exporters and firm-level data gives me some familiarity with how this evidence has held up. I flag that as familiarity, not as independent verification. The mechanism is also distinct from the 2008 prize for new trade theory. I do not treat the number of colleagues now preferring B048 as scientific merit. I changed because the discovery, attribution and maturity arguments favour it when I apply the same criteria I applied to B001.
statement.case_against: The main reservation is priority and attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Yeaple, developed parallel firm-level facts and models. As I recall, the Eaton-Kortum and Bernard et al. work is Ricardian or Bertrand with heterogeneous producers, not the monopolistic-competition selection model. None of them is on this ballot entry, so a Melitz-Helpman credit could be read as under-crediting the empirical foundations. The three-name cap cannot fix that, and I cannot settle the priority question from my recollection. The size of the welfare gains depends on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity. Helpman also appears in another candidate package (B026), which complicates how his credit is framed. I also see a real chance that B001 is the better choice. It created a field, and the gap is smaller than the opening and round-1 counts suggest. If the committee puts more weight on field creation than on tested core predictions, B001 is defensible, and I list it as my first alternative. My own field, industrial organisation and trade, is adjacent to B048, so I may be overconfident about how robust its firm-level evidence is.

responses.point: Hassler keeps B001 slightly ahead because he finds the creation of a new field somewhat more decisive than refinement within an established one. He calls the gap with B048 small, and he would word the B001 citation around measurable institutions and the investor-protection regularities, not the strong causal reading of legal origin.
responses.response: I made nearly the same argument in round 1 and still think it has force. Your wording would avoid endorsing the strong legal-origins claim, and that helps. Two things stop me from staying with B001. First, a field-creating contribution that has to be credited to three of its four core authors is a less clean prize than one where the two named people carry both the central model and its main extension. Second, the claim that survives the critiques is a body of regularities and a research design. That is a real contribution, but it is a weaker basis for a citation than a mechanism whose core predictions were tested directly and held up. I agree the gap is small and I do not think B001 would be a mistake. On the criteria we are all trying to apply equally, I now put B048 ahead.

responses.point: Strömberg argues that the critiques of the legal-origin coding and causal story qualify the mechanism more than they undermine the discovery. He says a prize can recognise the founding of a field even if the first causal story is only partly right. He names B049 or B048 as alternatives if the committee wants a cleaner identification record.
responses.response: I largely agree with that distinction, and it is why I do not think B001 is a weak candidate. If the committee accepts a citation built on the research design and established regularities, B001 stays competitive. But your own alternatives show where the real difficulty lies. If the committee leans toward identification and tested predictions, B048 is where it would go. The three-name cap and Vishny's exclusion cost something that I cannot argue away. Shleifer's separate prize-level work also makes it harder to keep the citation within law and finance. I take your point that conduct controversies cannot be assessed from the evidence supplied, and I leave them out of my reasoning. The move to B048 rests on attribution and robustness, not on any such concern.

responses.point: Dreber ranks B048 first because its core predictions have survived testing across countries and datasets. She ranks B001 seventh because measurement, coding and causal identification are weaker than its influence suggests. She also argues that field rotation and the 2008 prize are not scientific evidence.
responses.response: In round 1 I said the critique was the main reason my confidence in B001 was only moderate, and I now give it more weight. My view that the critique is part of what maturity means still stands. But maturity also means judging how the central claim fared, and here the two candidates differ. Core predictions of the firm-heterogeneity framework held up, and the main dispute is over magnitudes. The central causal claim in B001 is the part still in dispute. I agree that the 2008 prize and field rotation should not count against B048, because new trade theory with representative firms was a different discovery. I would still not rank B001 as low as seventh, and I keep it as an alternative.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson calls the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum line the real vulnerability for B048, because it concerns priority on the empirical foundations and not only a later extension. She proposes drafting the citation around the selection mechanism and gains-from-trade framework so that it does not overclaim the firm-level facts.
responses.response: I agree this is the main weakness of my new preferred configuration. It is the thing that could move me back if colleagues showed me that the priority question is more serious than I now think. My citation wording follows your suggestion. It refers to firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting shaping the gains from trade, and it does not claim the empirical firm-level facts as the discovery. That is, I think, the fair answer to the chair's question on whether mechanism-limited wording would suffice for me. It would. I also accept that this reduces the width of what is recognised. I regard that as an honest limit, not a free one.

responses.point: Fredriksson moved from B015 to B048 because the three-name credit for B015 is more contested and overlaps with recent prizes. He keeps B015 as an alternative and rejects a maturity objection to the China-shock papers.
responses.response: I agree with where you ended up on B048. I also agree B015 deserves to stay on the table as an alternative, and my round-1 view was that it would be a credible outcome if the committee puts identification credibility first. I have no strong view on the maturity objection. My reservation is attribution. The task framework draws on scholars outside the credited set, and the cap forces a choice between Katz and Dorn. I do not see a three-name citation for B015 that avoids that choice. That is why it is my second alternative and not my preferred part.

uncertainties: Whether the priority of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and Yeaple is serious enough that a Melitz-Helpman credit would be judged incomplete, and whether mechanism-limited wording answers it.
Whether B001 should rank above B048 if the committee prizes field creation and the research design over tested core predictions. I think the gap is small.
How Helpman's appearance on B026 should affect his credit here. I treat it as a reason to word the citation tightly, but I have not resolved it.
How much the welfare conclusions depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity.

Whether my familiarity with the firm-level trade and pricing literature makes me overconfident about B048. All my assessments rest on my own recollection of the literature and are not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Melitz, Helpman or the credited names of the alternatives B001 and B015 is apparent from my profile. I disclose, without adjudicating, that my spouse is Magdalena Andersson, a Swedish politician. That is a public fact with no apparent bearing on these candidates. I have co-authored with committee colleagues John Hassler and Tore Ellingsen on price-setting research unrelated to any candidate. My field, industrial organisation and trade, is adjacent to B048, and I have tried to apply the same criteria to B001 and B048. I moved my preference from B001 to B048 in this round, and my profile shows no connection to any credited candidate on either.
